head.h1: Diwali Catering in Dubai — Real Prices, Menus and Timings

opening_paragraph: Diwali catering in Dubai costs from AED 90 per person dropped off and AED 700 to 950 with a chef cooking on site. myCHEF covers the whole festival of lights table, from the diyas to the mithai counter. A private diwali chef in Dubai designs the spread, cooks in your kitchen, serves and clears away, so you sit with your family instead of running the evening. Send the date, the numbers and the venue, and during our published business hours you'll have a proposal you can read back promptly. This is diwali catering built around your home, not a fixed banquet menu shipped in from a hotel.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What does Diwali catering in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: Full-service diwali catering in Dubai includes everything from the first menu conversation to the last cleared plate, so you host and we handle the rest. That means bespoke menu design around your family's regional tastes, a chef cooking fresh on site, service staff who plate and refill, all the serveware and chafing dishes, and a kitchen left cleaner than we found it. Most diwali catering services in Dubai are fully vegetarian by default, with sattvic, Jain and no-onion-no-garlic options built in for the pooja day. We can add live chaat and dosa counters, a mithai and dessert table, welcome drinks, and rangoli-friendly styling for the table. Because myCHEF is a network of vetted chefs instead of a single kitchen, a diwali catering company match is made for your specific menu. You get someone who genuinely cooks the food you want on the night, not a generalist filling a slot.
How much does Diwali catering cost in Dubai?

From AED 90 per person for a dropped-off spread, AED 120 for a staffed buffet and AED 150 with live chaat or dosa counters. A chef cooking and plating on site is AED 700 to 950 per person. Minimums are 10 guests on volume formats, 20 on a buffet and AED 900 on order value, with 5% VAT added.
What's included in Diwali catering?
Everything from menu planning to the chef, the service staff, the plating and the cleanup. One team covers all of it, in your home, villa or office.
Can you cater a corporate Diwali event?
Yes. Corporate Diwali catering in Dubai runs from office desk lunches to full gala evenings, with live counters, timed service and invoicing your finance team can process.
Do you offer vegetarian and Jain Diwali menus?
Yes. Most Diwali menus are fully vegetarian by default, and we build Jain, vegan, gluten-free and no-onion-no-garlic versions without losing the festive spread.
Do you provide Diwali sweets and mithai?
Yes. A mithai and dessert counter of kaju katli, gulab jamun, jalebi and ladoo is part of nearly every Diwali order, made fresh instead of bought in.
How far ahead should I book Diwali catering?

As guidance: 72 hours for a standard package, 3 to 5 days once live counters or multi-staff service are involved, and 5 to 7 days for a bespoke menu or a larger private event. Diwali week itself fills first, so send that date as early as you can. Short-notice requests are assessed individually.
Which areas of Dubai do you serve?
All of Dubai, including Downtown, Business Bay, Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, Jumeirah, Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills, with the chef coming to your home or venue.
Can you do Diwali catering for a small party?

Yes. A dropped-off spread starts at 10 guests and AED 90 per person, with an AED 900 minimum order. A private chef has no minimum headcount at all, at AED 700 to 950 per person, which suits a family pooja for six or eight better than a buffet does.
Is there a Diwali catering price list?

Yes, by format: AED 90 per person dropped off, AED 120 for a staffed buffet, AED 150 with live chaat or dosa counters, and AED 700 to 950 for a chef cooking and plating on site. Minimums are 10 guests, 20 on a buffet, AED 900 on order value. Every quote is itemised on top of that.
For diwali catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .

MyCHEF arranges diwali catering dubai-wide, matched to your occasion, guest count and venue, in homes, villas, offices and event spaces. We regularly cook Diwali across Downtown Dubai, Business Bay, Dubai Marina, JBR, Palm Jumeirah, Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills, Emirates Hills and JVC, and the wider communities where families gather for the festival. A diwali caterer in Dubai from our network comes to you, so the celebration stays where your family already is. add_block.new_heading: What's on a Dubai Diwali menu?
new_paragraphs: A diwali menu in Dubai is yours to shape, and the best spreads balance North and South Indian classics with live theatre and a generous sweet finish. On the mains, think dal makhani, paneer three ways, chole bhature, biryani and a rotating South Indian section of dosa, idli and sambar. A live chaat counter of pani puri, dahi puri and samosa chaat gives guests something to gather around while the mains hold. The mithai counter is where Diwali earns its name, with kaju katli, gulab jamun, jalebi, motichoor ladoo and rasmalai, made fresh instead of bought in. Every diwali food catering menu is bespoke, so treat these as a starting point we tune to your region, your guests and any dietary needs. Regional requests are welcome, whether Gujarati, Punjabi, South Indian or Marwari. Tell the chef the home you're cooking for and the menu follows.

A chef cooking and plating through the evening is AED 700 to 950 per person. Volume formats need 10 guests, a full buffet 20, and the minimum order value is AED 900, with 5% VAT added. If you are pricing cheap diwali catering in Dubai, that AED 90 tier is our entry price, and the same kitchen cooks it. Guest count matters too, because larger numbers usually bring the per-head diwali catering price in Dubai down. For most home celebrations, families land between an affordable diwali catering spread and a mid-range live-counter package, while corporate galas and luxury diwali catering in Dubai run higher for premium ingredients and fuller service. There are no hidden line items, and your quote is itemised so you see exactly what each part of the diwali catering cost in Dubai covers. new_paragraphs: Not every Diwali is a hundred people. A pooja at home, one family, six or eight at the table is the most common booking of the week, and a buffet is the wrong shape for it. Small party catering in Dubai for Diwali works two ways. A dropped-off vegetarian spread starts at 10 guests and AED 90 per person, with the minimum order at AED 900, and you serve it yourself between the pooja and the sweets. Or a chef comes to the kitchen with no minimum headcount at all, at AED 700 to 950 per person, which is what most small Indian home celebrations pick: fresh puris, a live dosa pan, and mithai finished in front of the children. Small party catering in Dubai for Indian menus is easier than most cuisines to do well at low numbers, because the food is built for sharing plates instead of individual covers.

add_block.new_heading: Diwali restaurant, or Diwali at home?
new_paragraphs: Some of the searches that land here want a Diwali restaurant in Dubai: a table booked, a festive set menu, someone else's dining room for the night. That is a fair choice, and no caterer replaces it. What a restaurant cannot do is the pooja, the diyas on your own balcony, the rangoli at your door and the aunties in the kitchen. Diwali at home is a different evening, and catering exists so you can have that one without cooking for thirty people. The chef arrives with the menu you approved, cooks in your kitchen, and leaves it clean. You stay where your family already is.
